findings.title: Lint configs are written without the ownership check every other install write goes through
findings.description: `LintCheck.writeOrSuggest` and the ruff branch at `lint.ts:151` call `fs.writeFileSync` directly against `ctx.targetRoot`. Every other file the installer writes goes through `ctx.manifest.installFile`, which refuses to overwrite a file the guide does not own (`manifest.ts:130-176`) and backs the file up first. The lint path bypasses both: a pre-existing user-authored `ruff.toml` is never overwritten (the code checks `isFile` first), but a file the user created *after* a previous install is silently clobbered by the write path in the `python()` branch — `writeOrSuggest` is only reached when the config is absent, so the risk is bounded, yet `analysis_options.yaml` and `eslint.config.mjs` are written with `fs.writeFileSync` and no backup, and the written files are explicitly "not in the manifest and never pruned" (`lint.ts:10-11`). This means a user who edits a generated `eslint.config.mjs` loses the edit on the next `--write-lint` run with no warning and no backup, unlike `CLAUDE.md`, which is backed up to `<name>.pre-context-forge`. The AGENTS.md convention ("Fail explicitly", "never use cheap hacks") and the installer's own ownership model argue for routing these writes through the same backup/ownership path, or at minimum backing them up.

findings.title: `rules.exclude` is read per checkout, but the key's scope is `Shared` — the per-worktree read contradicts the config semantics
findings.description: `readRulesExclude(root)` constructs `new ConfigManager(root)` per root, so each worktree gets its own value from `<worktree>/.context-forge.toml`, falling back to the user config. But `rules.exclude` is declared `scope: ConfigScope.Shared` in `packages/core/src/config/ConfigKeys.ts:167`, and `ConfigManager.get` for a shared key reads the project file then the *user* file — there is no per-checkout resolution beyond that. The docstring "a worktree can carry its own" is therefore true only because a shared key may still be written into a worktree's `.context-forge.toml`. The comment in `installWorktrees` ("each with its own root and its own rules.exclude") and the test `reads rules.exclude for each worktree root` codify behavior that the config key's declared scope does not describe. Either the key should be `Personal`/per-checkout or the per-worktree read should be documented as an intentional extension in `ConfigKeys.ts`, so the two places do not drift.

findings.title: A failing root install aborts before worktrees, but a failing worktree install is reported only after all worktrees run — with no distinction between "failed" and "aborted"
findings.description: `installWorktrees` treats any non-zero `exitCode` as a worktree failure and continues. `installIde` returns `exitCode: 1` for `InstallAbort` *and* for filesystem errors (`installer.ts:88-96`), but the two mean different things: an `InstallAbort` (e.g. "rules source directory not found") will abort identically in every worktree, since they all share the guide directory. The loop will therefore run N identical failing installs and report N failures, when the root cause is one shared precondition. The old code had the same shape for worktrees but the root was a separate process whose exit code was surfaced distinctly. Consider checking the shared precondition (guide present, rules dir present) once before the loop, and distinguishing abort-vs-error in the worktree report.

findings.title: The dry-run sandbox copies entire top-level directories, so unrelated project files are copied and diffed
findings.description: `copyInstallPaths` copies `.claude`, `.cursor`, `.github`, `.agents` and `.context-forge` recursively into a temp sandbox with `verbatimSymlinks: true`. The `.claude` directory in a real project can contain `settings.local.json`, `worktrees/` (excluded via the `filter`), history, and caches; `.github` can contain workflows, issue templates, and Actions directories. All of that is copied on every dry run, then walked by `listInstallFiles` on both roots and compared byte-for-byte (`sameContent` reads every file in full). On a large repository this makes `--dry-run` slow and memory-hungry, and the diff is reported over paths the installer never touches. The `DRY_RUN_SKIP_PATH` filter only excludes `.claude/worktrees`. Narrowing the copied set to the paths the installer actually writes (as `harness.ts` `INSTALL_PATHS` approximates) would keep the preview accurate and cheap.

findings.title: Dry-run diff output is not sorted consistently with the "byte order" claim in its own doc comment
findings.description: `reportChanges` claims each group is "in byte order", and `listInstallFiles` does sort by `byteOrder`. But the three groups are emitted in the order added / modified / removed, and within each group the entries inherit `after`/`before` order — which is byte order. That part is consistent. The actual drift is in the *file* comment on `dryRun.ts:1-5`: "install into a sandbox copy of the project's install paths, then report what would be added, changed and removed" — but the sandbox install also writes a manifest into the sandbox (`.context-forge/<target>.manifest`), and `INSTALL_PATHS` includes `MANIFEST_DIR`, so the manifest shows up as an "added" file in every fresh dry run (visible in `test_flags_dry_run_fresh.snap`: `+ .context-forge/claude.manifest`). A user reading "Preview the files setup-ide would add" sees a manifest they never asked about. This is arguably correct, but the dry-run report and the CLI's `--dry-run` help text ("Preview the files setup-ide would add, change, or remove") do not mention it.

findings.title: `installWorktrees` installs into worktrees without the overwrite prompt the root gets
findings.description: The root install asks before overwriting unmanaged marker files. Worktree installs do not: `installCheckout` is called directly for each worktree, so a worktree containing an unmanaged `CLAUDE.md` is overwritten without asking. In the old code this was safe because propagation only *copied* the root's already-installed output into worktrees. Now each worktree runs a full install, which can overwrite user content in that worktree. The `InstallManifest.installFile` ownership check limits this to files the manifest claims, but for a worktree with no manifest (or a stale one), the first install can legitimately claim ownership of a user file. The root's prompt-and-backup treatment should apply per worktree, or the asymmetry should be documented.

findings.title: `MANAGED_MARKER_END` and `GENERATED_MARKER` are exported from `ideTargets.ts` but the module comment no longer describes them
findings.description: The module header says the file "holds the per-target descriptors and every marker literal", which is accurate, but `MANAGED_MARKER_END` is only consumed by `ideInstall/managedSection.ts` and `GENERATED_MARKER` only by `ideInstall/targets/copilot.ts`. Both are now installer-internal, while `ideTargets.ts` is otherwise the command-layer vocabulary. Not wrong, but the layering (installer importing from `commands/`) is worth a deliberate decision rather than an accident of where the literal first lived.

findings.title: `ConfigManager.get` returns `string | boolean | number`, so the `typeof value !== 'string'` guard in `readRulesExclude` is defensive but unreachable
findings.description: `rules.exclude` is declared `type: 'string'` with `default: ''`, and `ConfigManager.get` returns `def.default` when unset, so the value is always a string for this key. The guard throws a plain `Error` (not `UserError`), so it would surface as `Error: rules.exclude resolved to a number...` rather than a user-facing message. It is cheap insurance against a future type change on the key; fine to keep, but consider `UserError` so the failure mode is a clean message rather than a generic one.

findings.title: The `getApplyTo` behavior change is a deliberate deviation from bash, correctly documented and re-pinned
findings.description: The `**\n**` double-default is now `**`, changing generated `applyTo:` values and the CRC in the manifest (visible in the updated snapshots `test_targets_copilot_fresh.snap` and `test_targets_copilot_prompts.snap`). The comment cites #40 and the test was renamed from "pins #40" to "gives the default once", which correctly signals an intentional fix rather than a rewritten test. This changes the content of already-installed `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md` files, so the next install will report those as modified — worth a CHANGELOG entry given the repo's versioning rules treat a changed artifact as user-facing.

findings.title: `replaceBlock` drops the final newline using a `slice(0, -1)` on the merged text
findings.description:
The fix for #38 is correct for the "original had no trailing newline" case, but the guard is `original === '' || original.endsWith('
')`. An `original` that is empty yields `merged` (block content), which ends with `
` — correct. An `original` ending in `
` yields `merged` unchanged — correct. The `slice` branch therefore only fires when the original genuinely lacked a final newline. The logic is right; it is just worth noting that `merged` is guaranteed non-empty in that branch (the block always contributes at least the BEGIN marker), so the `slice` cannot produce an empty string.

findings.title: The `any` ban and strict typing are respected throughout
findings.description: No `any`, no `as` assertions beyond the two pre-existing `as string | boolean | number` casts in `ConfigManager`, and no empty catch blocks in the new code. `Record<Language, () => void>` and `Record<Target, ...>` are used to make an incomplete mapping a compile error, which matches the project's "define it once" rule. The new files are all well under the 300-line guideline (`lint.ts` is 239 lines, `dryRun.ts` is 124).
